cases.answer: A namespace is a mapping from names to objects. [1] Most are currently implemented as Python dictionaries. [2] Examples include the built-in names, the global names in a module, and the local names in a function invocation. [3] Names in different namespaces have no relation to each other. [4]
cited: web-python-docs: A *namespace* is a mapping from names to objects.
web-python-docs: Most namespaces are currently implemented as Python dictionaries, but that’s normally not noticeable in any way (except for performance), and it may change in the future.

web-python-docs: the set of built-in names (containing functions such as [`abs()`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#abs "abs"), and built-in exception names); the global names in a module; and the local names in a function invocation.
web-python-docs: The important thing to know about namespaces is that there is absolutely no relation between names in different namespaces;

cases.answer: Python does name mangling: an identifier like `__spam` is textually replaced with `_classname__spam`, where `classname` is the current class name with leading underscores stripped [1]. This happens wherever the identifier appears inside the class definition, whatever its syntactic position [2].
cited: web-python-docs: Any identifier of the form `__spam` (at least two leading underscores, at most one trailing underscore) is textually replaced with `_classname__spam`, where `classname` is the current class name with leading underscore(s) stripped.
web-python-docs: This mangling is done without regard to the syntactic position of the identifier, as long as it occurs within the definition of a class.

cases.answer: When there are no more elements, `__next__()` raises a `StopIteration` exception [1]. That exception tells the `for` loop to terminate [1].

cases.answer: A namespace in Python is a mapping that connects names to objects.[1] Names in separate namespaces are independent: two modules can both define a function called `maximize`, and prefixing it with the module name distinguishes them.[2]
cited: web-python-docs: A *namespace* is a mapping from names to objects.

web-python-docs: The important thing to know about namespaces is that there is absolutely no relation between names in different namespaces; for instance, two different modules may both define a function `maximize` without confusion — users of the modules must prefix it with the module name.
